deep.reconstruction:
Context: on the preceding pages Grothendieck works with a 'norme de Schatten' N on R^(N). In modern terms this is a symmetric gauge (norming) function in the sense of von Neumann and Schatten. To it he attaches two sequence spaces. The maximal one, ℓ^N, consists of x ∈ ℓ^∞ with N(x) = sup_n N(|x|_n) < ∞. The minimal one, ℓ_N, is the closure of finitely supported sequences in ℓ^N. He has shown ℓ^1 ⊂ ℓ_N ⊂ c_0 and defined the polar norm N'(y) = sup_{N(x)≤1} |<x,y>|, which is again a Schatten norm.

This page:
(10) Hölder inequality. Σ|x_i x'_i| ≤ N(x) N'(x'). Proof: on truncations, Σ_{i≤n} |x_i x'_i| = <|x|_n, |x'|_n> ≤ N(|x|_n) N'(|x'|_n), then take the sup over n. The pairing ℓ^N × ℓ^{N'} → R is therefore bilinear and of norm ≤ 1.

Duality theorem. The dual of ℓ_N is exactly ℓ^{N'}, isometrically. Proof sketch on the page:
- Restrict a continuous functional X' on ℓ_N to ℓ^1, or to the finitely supported sequences.
- It is then given by some x' ∈ ℓ^∞.
- Testing on truncations gives N'(|x'|_n) ≤ ||X'||, hence N'(x') ≤ ||X'||.
- Density of R^(N) in ℓ_N finishes the argument.
He remarks that the dual of ℓ^N is in general not ℓ^{N'}, because ℓ_N need not be dense in ℓ^N. Example: N = N_∞, where ℓ_N = c_0 and ℓ^N = ℓ^∞.

Reflexivity criterion. ℓ_N is reflexive iff ℓ_N = ℓ^N and ℓ_{N'} = ℓ^{N'}. He argues through a cycle of implications:
- ℓ_N reflexive ⇒ its dual ℓ^{N'} is reflexive.
- Then ℓ_{N'}, a closed subspace of ℓ^{N'}, is reflexive, so its dual ℓ^N is reflexive.
- From this he gets equalities: ℓ_{N'}, closed in the dual ℓ^{N'} of ℓ_N, coincides with it, and similarly ℓ_N = ℓ^N.
- Conversely, if both equalities hold, (ℓ_N)' = ℓ^{N'} = ℓ_{N'} and (ℓ_{N'})' = ℓ^N = ℓ_N, so ℓ_N equals its bidual.

New definition. For Banach spaces E, F and a Schatten norm N, let L^N(E,F) be the set of u ∈ L(E,F) whose sequence of numbers (f_i(u)) lies in ℓ^N, with N(u) = N((f_i(u))) < ∞ (formula (11)). The f_i(u) are presumably defined earlier in the manuscript; given the next page they are approximation-type (s-)numbers. The next page shows N(u) is a norm with the ideal property, and that L_N(E,F) is the closure of E'⊗F. It also proves the composition inequality N(vu) ≤ N'(u) N''(v) whenever N(xy) ≤ N'(x) N''(y).

Purpose: to build symmetrically normed operator ideals between Banach spaces, generalising Schatten's classes on Hilbert space. This feeds the tensor-product / nuclear-operator programme of the 1953–55 work.
errors: The trailing 'q' in (10) (and in the following line) seems to be a stray mark or misreading; the inequality should simply be Σ|x_i x'_i| ≤ N(x)N'(x').

The reflexivity argument is compressed: the step 'ℓ_{N'} reflexive ⇒ ℓ^N reflexive' needs (ℓ_{N'})' = ℓ^{N''} = ℓ^N, i.e. N'' = N. This holds for norms in this setting but is not stated on this page (a margin of the previous page mentions it). The equality step, from reflexivity of the dual to equality of ℓ_N and ℓ^N, is only sketched (a non-dense closed subspace would give a functional not coming from ℓ^{N'}).

ideas.what: Hölder inequality between a symmetric norm and its polar on sequences
ideas.modern_name: Hölder inequality for Köthe dual / associate norms

ideas.what: Dual of the minimal symmetric sequence space ℓ_N is the maximal space ℓ^{N'} of the polar norm
ideas.modern_name: Köthe duality for symmetric sequence spaces; (S_Φ^{(0)})* = S_{Φ*}

ideas.what: ℓ_N reflexive iff ℓ_N = ℓ^N and ℓ_{N'} = ℓ^{N'}
ideas.modern_name: Reflexivity criterion for symmetric (Köthe) sequence spaces: both the norm and its associate are order continuous
ideas.usually_credited_to: Schatten; Gohberg–Krein; Lozanovskii / Luxemburg–Zaanen for Banach lattices

ideas.what: Operator classes L^N(E,F) between arbitrary Banach spaces, defined by membership of an s-number-type sequence in a symmetric sequence space ℓ^N
ideas.modern_name: Symmetrically normed operator ideals on Banach spaces via approximation/s-numbers, S_Φ^{app}
ideas.usually_credited_to: Pietsch (1963 onward, s-numbers and operator ideals); Schatten and Calkin for Hilbert space
ideas.where_published: Possibly partially echoed in Produits tensoriels topologiques (Memoirs AMS 16, 1955) and in work on the Fredholm theory; not certain

missed.claim: In 1953 Grothendieck sets up general symmetric-norm operator classes L^N(E,F) between Banach spaces. They come with minimal (L_N) and maximal (L^N) versions, a duality theory and (next page) a Hölder-type composition inequality. This anticipates Pietsch's s-number operator ideals of the 1960s. Whether this general Schatten-norm framework appears in Grothendieck's published work is unclear.

missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical priority: it shows Grothendieck working with general symmetrically normed operator ideals on Banach spaces about a decade before Pietsch's systematic theory. The mathematics itself is now standard.

deep.surprise_reason: The sequence-space duality and reflexivity results on this page are standard (Schatten, Köthe) and essentially routine. The mildly notable point is the early (1953) definition of general Schatten-norm operator classes between Banach spaces, which anticipates later operator-ideal theory. Even so, the precise meaning of f_i(u) is not visible here, and nothing is mathematically new today.
